{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The PUT /tasks/{id} endpoint violates strict PUT semantics: it requires 'title' and 'status' but leaves 'description' optional. In a true PUT (full replacement), omitting an optional field implies deleting it, which is likely unintended. This should either be a PATCH endpoint or all fields must be required.",
    "The Task definition includes 'created_at' but omits 'updated_at', which is a critical field for task management to track when status or details were last modified.",
    "The GET /tasks endpoint lacks query parameters for filtering (e.g., by status) and sorting. Combined with the explicit omission of pagination, this makes the list endpoint highly impractical for real-world usage.",
    "Path parameters (like 'id') are defined inside the 'request_schema' object without distinguishing them from the request body. Standard API specifications (like OpenAPI) separate path/query parameters from the request body schema."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Change PUT to PATCH and make all fields in the request schema optional, or keep PUT and make 'description' required to enforce full resource replacement.",
    "Add an 'updated_at' field with 'date-time' format to the Task definition.",
    "Define a 'query_schema' or 'parameters' array for GET /tasks to allow filtering by 'status' and sorting by 'created_at'.",
    "Adopt an OpenAPI-style structure that separates 'parameters' (path, query) from 'requestBody' to ensure compatibility with standard API code generators."
  ]
}
